scope: All verified named simulator platforms in the benchmark catalog, plus four explicitly used robot-learning frameworks. Not an exhaustive catalog of robotics simulation software.

simulators.name: MuJoCo
simulators.description: Articulated dynamics and contact for manipulation, locomotion and model-based control.
simulators.note: General-purpose articulated models; concrete assets, actuators and task definitions come from environment packages. MJX and MuJoCo Warp provide related acceleration paths. Open-sourced May 2022; the milestone here is the original 2012 paper.

paper.title: MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control
paper.note: Count applies to this selected reference paper, not all papers in the ecosystem.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Introduction; articulated structures, contact, model formats and project history.
Curated robot models include arms, hands, humanoids and quadrupeds.

simulators.name: PyBullet / Bullet
simulators.description: Python-accessible collision and rigid-body dynamics, robot control and reinforcement-learning environments.
simulators.note: PyBullet is the Python robotics interface to Bullet, rather than a separate physics engine. The repository contains the broader Bullet SDK and examples.

release.basis: Beginning of the 2016–2021 software citation supplied by maintainers (year precision).

paper.note: Maintainers provide a software citation (Coumans and Bai, 2016–2021); no selected indexed paper citation count is recorded.

github.scope: Entire Bullet Physics SDK repository; not PyBullet alone.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.

simulators.name: SAPIEN
simulators.description: Articulated-object interaction, robot manipulation, visual rendering and depth-sensor simulation.
simulators.note: SAPIEN supplies physics and rendering; environments such as ManiSkill implement robots and tasks above it. CPU/GPU and rendering features depend on the version.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

paper.title: SAPIEN: A SimulAted Part-Based Interactive ENvironment
paper.note: Count applies to this selected reference paper, not all papers in the ecosystem.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
SAPIEN 3 features and user guide.
Examples built on SAPIEN across multiple embodiments.

simulators.name: CoppeliaSim / V-REP
simulators.description: Scene-based robot prototyping, kinematics, dynamics, sensors and industrial automation.
simulators.note: A robot simulator with switchable physics plugins. Newton Dynamics is distinct from the newer NVIDIA/DeepMind/Disney Newton engine. A benchmark using CoppeliaSim does not establish which physics plugin it uses.

release.basis: V-REP 3.0.0 open-source milestone; the CoppeliaSim name was introduced later.

paper.title: V-REP: A versatile and scalable robot simulation framework
paper.note: Counts the original V-REP framework paper, before the CoppeliaSim rename.

github.scope: CoppeliaSim core library; other plugins and binaries are distributed separately.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Supported dynamics engines.
Version history and robot model examples.

simulators.name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
simulators.description: Robot and sensor simulation, photorealistic rendering, synthetic data and ROS integration.
simulators.note: Physics and rendering platform used by Isaac Lab and OmniGibson. Current documentation lists PhysX and Newton; older benchmark editions generally pin a particular Isaac Sim/PhysX stack. Backend availability is version-dependent.

release.basis: Documented Omniverse robotics edition milestone; earlier Isaac SDK simulators predate this.

paper.note: The official project supplies a software citation. No paper citation count is recorded; an independent Isaac Sim survey would measure a different work.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Current platform overview and available backends.
Wheeled robots, manipulators and policy-controlled robots.
Official citation metadata identifies software, not a research paper.

simulators.name: NVIDIA Isaac Gym
simulators.description: GPU-parallel robot physics with tensor-based reinforcement-learning rollouts.
simulators.note: Standalone research SDK predating Isaac Lab. The linked repository supplies example environments rather than the simulator SDK itself. Preserve the simulator version when interpreting older results.

paper.title: Isaac Gym: High Performance GPU-Based Physics Simulation For Robot Learning
paper.note: Count applies to this selected reference paper, not all papers in the ecosystem.

github.scope: IsaacGymEnvs example environments; not the SDK distribution.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Preview announcement, PhysX and tensor interface.

simulators.name: Habitat-Sim
simulators.description: Indoor navigation, rearrangement and embodied interaction in scanned or synthetic scenes.
simulators.note: Simulation backend of the Habitat ecosystem. Rendered sensors and optional Bullet rigid/articulated physics support different tasks; the selected original Habitat paper does not describe every later feature.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

paper.title: Habitat: A Platform for Embodied AI Research
paper.note: Counts the original Habitat platform paper (2019), not the sum of Habitat 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 citations.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Habitat ecosystem, navigation, manipulation and human–robot interaction.

simulators.name: AI2-THOR
simulators.description: Interactive indoor scenes for navigation, object interaction, rearrangement and visual reasoning.
simulators.note: Built with Unity and its PhysX-based physics. Embodiment depends on the track: default agents use abstract actions; RoboTHOR targets navigation, and ManipulaTHOR adds an arm. Supporting a track does not imply all tasks accept every robot.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

paper.title: AI2-THOR: An Interactive 3D Environment for Visual AI
paper.note: Count applies to this selected reference paper, not all papers in the ecosystem.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Arm-based manipulation track.
Navigation track.
Platform paper: Unity/physics architecture.

simulators.name: Genesis World (Genesis)
simulators.description: Parallel multi-physics simulation of rigid robots, deformable materials and fluids.
simulators.note: Previously named Genesis. Current repository integrates rigid, FEM, MPM and particle solvers, with rendering and a compiler. Solver support and differentiability vary; this is not evidence that every benchmark supports all solvers.

paper.note: Official citations refer to the software (December 2024) and a 2026 project blog post. No selected indexed paper count is recorded.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Quadruped and drone learning examples.

simulators.name: NVIDIA FleX
simulators.description: Unified particle simulation for cloth, soft bodies, fluids and rigid/deformable interactions.
simulators.note: A physics library rather than a complete robotics task framework. SoftGym supplies manipulation effectors and tasks above FleX; deformable objects are not themselves a soft-robot embodiment.

paper.title: Unified particle physics for real-time applications
paper.note: Counts the underlying unified-particle-physics paper; not a simulator-specific adoption count.

github.scope: FleX SDK/demo distribution repository; engine source and ecosystem usage are not captured by stars.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Underlying unified particle physics method.
Robotics manipulation environments using FleX.

simulators.name: Pymunk
simulators.description: 2D rigid-body dynamics for planar interaction, games and abstract manipulation tasks.
simulators.note: Python interface to Chipmunk2D. Push-T uses a planar abstract pushing effector; Pymunk is not a 3D articulated-robot simulator.

paper.note: No selected research paper or indexed citation count is recorded for this software.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Push-T environment implemented with Pymunk.

simulators.name: EvoGym simulator
simulators.description: 2D voxel-based soft-robot simulation for joint morphology and controller optimization.
simulators.note: Includes a task suite and its own soft-body simulator. Voxel morphology and 2D actuation differ from conventional articulated arms or humanoids.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

paper.title: Evolution Gym: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Evolving Soft Robots
paper.note: Counts the Evolution Gym benchmark-and-simulator paper; NeurIPS 2021 publication predates the January 2022 arXiv milestone.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.

simulators.name: DaXBench simulator
simulators.description: Differentiable deformable-object manipulation with fluid, rope and cloth environments.
simulators.note: DaXBench combines a benchmark and differentiable simulation framework. Its supplied tasks use simulated manipulation effectors; they do not establish a standard arm/hand asset library. The initial code release is documented as May 2023.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

paper.title: Benchmarking Deformable Object Manipulation with Differentiable Physics
paper.note: Counts the DaXBench benchmark-and-simulator paper; the release column records its first paper submission.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.

simulators.name: PlasticineLab simulator
simulators.description: Differentiable elasto-plastic material simulation for tool-based soft-object manipulation.
simulators.note: Uses simplified manipulation tools and deformable material. Material softness does not establish support for soft robot embodiments.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

paper.title: PlasticineLab: A Soft-Body Manipulation Benchmark with Differentiable Physics
paper.note: Count applies to this selected reference paper, not all papers in the ecosystem.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.
Project description, differentiable physics and tool-based tasks.
Method: differentiable material point simulation.

simulators.name: RoboEval symbolic simulator
simulators.description: Runs generated service-robot programs and checks symbolic temporal traces.
simulators.note: Models service-robot actions and their traces rather than continuous contacts, sensors or motor dynamics. The simulator is part of CodeBotler/RoboEval.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

paper.title: Deploying and Evaluating LLMs to Program Service Mobile Robots
paper.note: Counts the CodeBotler/RoboEval system paper; it includes both program generation and evaluation.

github.scope: Entire CodeBotler system and RoboEval repository.

sources.locator: Official repository documentation and examples; reviewed 2026-09-30.

simulators.name: NVIDIA Isaac Lab
simulators.description: Robot-learning environments, policy training, data collection and domain randomization.
simulators.note: Framework above Isaac Sim. Backends and robot assets depend on the release; the current main branch is development code. Benchmarks may use an optional Arena implementation alongside another simulator.

release.basis: Official Isaac Lab release announcement; evolved from ORBIT.

paper.title: Isaac Lab: A GPU-Accelerated Simulation Framework for Multi-Modal Robot Learning
paper.note: Count applies to this selected reference paper, not all papers in the ecosystem.

simulators.name: robosuite
simulators.description: Modular robots, controllers, sensors and manipulation environments above MuJoCo.
simulators.note: Provides robot composition and learning environments above MuJoCo. Humanoid and whole-body support is documented in v1.5; older LIBERO/RoboCasa stacks use their own pinned versions.

release.basis: First arXiv submission of the selected reference paper; not necessarily the first software release.

simulators.note: Powered by SAPIEN. The selected paper and milestone describe ManiSkill3; linked benchmark resources can use earlier ManiSkill2 or later versions with different assets and protocols.

simulators.note: Built on Isaac Sim for the BEHAVIOR ecosystem. Supports rigid/deformable objects, fluids and task predicates. The selected BEHAVIOR-1K paper covers the simulator together with the benchmark.
